status_note: APPROVED by the owner on 2026-10-18. The operator verified every corpus quote, and the owner confirmed the crop requirement unit kg/ha. Issue #57 may consume these constants. v2 separates per-part dry matter and per-nutrient release; the v1 single leaf dry-matter value and the single residue-N release value applied to N, P and K are superseded. The nutrition track sizes fresh material with the owner-approved no-overshoot rule (to the nutrient that needs the least), so no nutrient exceeds the target fraction.

owner_signoff.decision: Approved as in this file: every per-part dry-matter and per-nutrient release value, the plant-tea steep/dilution/application constants, the mulch depth and the WSP vinegar substitution. The crop requirement unit kg/ha is CONFIRMED by the owner.

formula.name: two-track nutrient-equivalence formula

tracks.nutrition: Fresh plant material needed to supply a target fraction of the crop's seasonal N, P and K requirement through chop-and-drop, mulch or plant tea. Per nutrient: fresh_kg = target_fraction * R * 0.1 * A / (T / 1000 * DM(part) * E(nutrient)). The owner-approved no-overshoot rule sizes the single applied mass to the nutrient that needs the LEAST material, so no nutrient exceeds the target fraction; each nutrient's coverage at that mass is reported with a top-up note for the shortfalls.
tracks.booster: The source FPJ/FFJ/WSP recipe made at the recipe's standard batch and standard dilution/application rate. The small nutrient amount it supplies is reported only as information; the booster track makes no requirement-coverage claim.

symbols.R: crop requirement midpoint for the nutrient, kg/ha
symbols.T: tissue midpoint for the nutrient, ppm on a dry-matter basis
symbols.DM: dry-matter fraction for the tissue's plant part, kg dry matter per kg fresh material
symbols.E: nutrient release/extraction fraction for the nutrient, kg plant-available nutrient per kg tissue nutrient
symbols.F: optional target fraction of the crop requirement, default 1.0

nutrition_steps: target_g = F * R * 0.1 * A   (1 kg/ha = 0.1 g/m2)
available_g_per_kg_fresh = T / 1000 * DM(part) * E(nutrient)   (ppm = mg/kg dry; /1000 gives g/kg dry)
sizing_nutrient = the nutrient with the SMALLEST fresh_plant_material_kg (no overshoot)

worked_example.input: Stinging Nettle for Tomato, 25 m2, target fraction 1.0
worked_example.note: Numbers are illustrative and rounded; the oracle output is authoritative. The no-overshoot rule sizes to N (the smallest per-nutrient need, about 9 kg/m2), which covers 100% of N but only about 12% of P and about 91% of K, so P and K carry top-up notes.

dry_matter_fraction.unit: kg dry matter per kg fresh plant material
dry_matter_fraction.used_in: available_g_per_kg_fresh for the nutrition track and the booster standard batch

source.quote: Assuming a medium leaf weight of 2 g fresh weight and a leaf water content of 85%.
source.derivation: 1 - 0.85 = 0.15 kg dry matter per kg fresh leaf; other parts use their own quote below.

leaf.quote: Assuming a medium leaf weight of 2 g fresh weight and a leaf water content of 85%.

herb.corpus_file: Integrated_Farming_Systems/Gaia_s Garden - A Guide to Home-Scale Permaculture.md
herb.derivation: 1 - 0.85 = 0.15 for whole herbs, soft shoots, seedlings and hay proxies.

fruit.quote: The ripe fruit of tomatoes is eaten raw or cooked. It is about 90% water
fruit.derivation: 1 - 0.90 = 0.10. Watery fruits range from about 90% to 96% water in the corpus (Mollison: 'Fruit is 96% water'), so 0.10 is the high-dry-matter end of the fruit range.

seed.corpus_file: Integrated_Farming_Systems/Edible Forest Gardens Vol.2 Design and Practice.md
seed.quote: Most seeds ripen at about 40% moisture content but get harvested at 20% or less moisture as the plant browns.
seed.derivation: 1 - 0.20 = 0.80 at harvest; stored seed is drier (about 13-14% moisture), so 0.80 is conservative.

root.quote: The DM content of most varieties selected for commercial usage ranges from about 18 to 26% (Burton, 1989)
root.derivation: Midpoint of 18-26% = 22% = 0.22 for roots, tubers and bulbs.

bark.quote: Moisture at harvest depends on tree age, ranging from about 55 percent at 1 year to 45 percent at 4 years and 35 percent at 7 years
bark.derivation: 1 - 0.35 = 0.65 for mature wood/bark; the corpus quote is for leucaena wood, used here as a bark proxy.

stem.corpus_file: Integrated_Farming_Systems/Industrial hemp (Cannabis sativa L.) for phytoremediation_ Energy and _environmental life cycle assessment of using contaminated biomass as an _energy resource.md
stem.quote: Fresh industrial hemp was harvested at blooming ... with an average dry matter content of 35%.
stem.derivation: 0.35 for fresh stems and pith, using whole fresh hemp biomass as the proxy.

flower.corpus_file: Integrated_Farming_Systems/Gaia_s Garden - A Guide to Home-Scale Permaculture.md
flower.derivation: 1 - 0.85 = 0.15 for fresh flowers and buds; no separate flower measurement was found in the corpus.

dry_matter_fraction.applies_to: every catalog part; unmapped parts fall back to the herb value and say so in the result
dry_matter_fraction.caveat: Each part value is a corpus-derived point estimate, not a measurement of the specific candidate. Bark uses a wood-moisture proxy and flower uses the whole-plant water content because the corpus has no separate measurement.

nutrient_release_fraction.unit: kg plant-available nutrient per kg tissue nutrient
nutrient_release_fraction.used_in: available_g_per_kg_fresh for the nutrition track and the booster standard batch

source.quote: In 1943, Norman and Werkman labeled soybeans with 15N. Addition of the labeled residue to soil showed that 26% of the tagged N was recovered by a subsequent crop.
source.derivation: N keeps the 0.26 labeled-residue recovery. P and K use separate sources below and do not reuse this N figure.

N.quote: In 1943, Norman and Werkman labeled soybeans with 15N. Addition of the labeled residue to soil showed that 26% of the tagged N was recovered by a subsequent crop.
N.caveat: A labeled soybean-residue recovery, not a measurement of a fermented plant extract.

P.quote: This is why, even with optimum management, the efficiency of plant uptake of phosphorus is very low usually less than 20 percent.
P.derivation: Use 0.20 as an upper-bound phosphorus availability proxy: less than 20% of applied phosphorus is typically taken up.
P.caveat: This is a plant-uptake efficiency, not a residue-release measurement. It is proposed as a conservative proxy because the corpus gives no direct P release fraction for mulch or fermented plant material; a residue-specific P mineralization measurement should replace it.

K.corpus_file: Natural_Fertilizers/Trees, Crops & Soil Fertility - G. Schroth, F. Sinclair.md
K.quote: This fraction includes most of the potassium, and for freshly cut (as opposed to naturally fallen) materials it may also include a relevant percentage of the phosphorus in the biomass
K.derivation: Most potassium is rapidly leached from fresh litter and mulch; use 0.80.
K.caveat: The corpus says 'most' rather than a measured percentage, and the same passage notes that little is known about the fate of the leached potassium. 0.80 is the owner-approved value (2026-10-18).

nutrient_release_fraction.applies_to: N, P and K separately; never one shared residue-N figure
nutrient_release_fraction.caveat: N and K have residue/litter evidence; P uses a plant-uptake efficiency as a conservative proxy. All three are approved by the owner (2026-10-18).

sugar_to_plant_material_ratio.unit: kg brown sugar per kg fresh plant material

source.quote: Mix the ingredients with brown sugar in a 1:1 ratio for storage.
source.app_recipe_corroboration: Enriched_Recipes.json FPJ and FFJ steps: 'Mix the chopped shoots/fruits with brown sugar in a 1:1 ratio by weight.'

sugar_to_plant_material_ratio.caveat: The KNF text also allows 1/2 to 2/3 sugar by weight for immediate use; v2 follows the app recipes' 1:1 storage ratio.

source.quote: Put the bones in the jar with BRV (charcoal: BRV= 1:10).

vinegar_to_material_ratio.applies_to: WSP, where v2 substitutes the candidate plant material for bones and flags the substitution
vinegar_to_material_ratio.caveat: The corpus ratio is for bone charcoal in brown rice vinegar. The app's WSP uses bones plus vinegar and says 'until submerged'; v2 uses the WSP/WCP 1:10 ratio. The plant-material substitution is a derived proposal, not a source recipe.

ferment_density_kg_per_l.used_in: converting concentrate mass to volume in the booster standard batch

source.quote: Water-density approximation used to convert a plant/sugar or plant/vinegar mixture to litres.

ferment_density_kg_per_l.caveat: Sugar solutions and plant extracts are denser than water; v2 treats 1 kg as 1 L so the dilution arithmetic is transparent. This is a unit convention, not a corpus-derived dosing constant.

source.corpus_file: Organic_Farming/hemp diseases and pests-management and biological control by-jim-mcpartland-r-c-clarke.md
source.quote: Fibre production requires high soil N, at least 150 kg ha-1.
source.app_data_corroboration: Crop_Requirements.json stores ranges such as Rice Nitrogen 60-100, Phosphorus 35-58, Potassium 36-44, consistent with kg/ha recommendations.

crop_requirement_unit.caveat: Crop_Requirements.json does not state a unit in the file, but the owner CONFIRMED kg/ha on 2026-10-18; the values and the corpus convention are kg/ha.

source.quote: Use the midpoint of the crop's declared NPK range, matching bioaccumulator_oracle.py.

crop_requirement_midpoint.caveat: A midpoint is a central estimate, not a lower or upper recommendation.

source.quote: Leaf spraying: Dilute M-B or M-C in the ratio of 1/1,000. Spray 200~300 l per 100a on the leaves.

foliar_application_rate_l_per_ha.caveat: The quote is for mineral liquids M-B/M-C, not FPJ/FFJ. It defines the standard-rate booster volume; the booster makes no requirement-coverage claim.

source.quote: Soil irrigation: Dilute M-B or M-C in the ratio of 1/1,000. Water 1~2 tons of M-B or M-C per 100a.
source.derivation: Midpoint of 1-2 t per 100a; 100a = 1 ha and 1 t = 1000 L.

soil_drench_application_rate_l_per_ha.caveat: The quote is for mineral liquids M-B/M-C, not FPJ/FFJ. It defines the standard-rate booster volume; the booster makes no requirement-coverage claim.

plant_tea_steep_water_l_per_kg.unit: L water per kg fresh plant material

source.quote: Simply fill an old pillowcase or burlap bag with your chosen material (comfrey, nettles, compost or manure) and sink it into a large bucket or barrel of water.
source.derivation: The corpus says to cover the material with water but gives no numeric material:water ratio. v2 proposes 10 L water per kg fresh material so the tea volume is transparent and testable; this is the one steep-ratio convention in the proposal.

plant_tea_steep_water_l_per_kg.caveat: A method convention proposed for arithmetic transparency, not a corpus measurement. Approved by the owner (2026-10-18).

plant_tea_dilution_ratio.unit: L water per L finished tea concentrate

source.quote: The liquid feed must be diluted before it is applied to plants at a ratio of about 10 parts water to 1 part concentrate.

plant_tea_dilution_ratio.caveat: The corpus recipe is comfrey tea; the same dilution is proposed for a candidate-plant tea. JADAM's JLF standard is a different, much weaker 1:100 dilution.

source.corpus_file: Natural_Fertilizers/JADAM Organic FarmingmThe way to UltraLowCost agriculture.md
source.quote: Standard is ×100 dilution. Calculate the volume of liquid fertilizer based on 1 t (264 gal) of water being used for 0.03 ha (0.08 ac).
source.derivation: 1000 L diluted liquid per 0.03 ha = 1000 / 300 m2 = 3.333 L/m2.

plant_tea_application_rate_l_per_m2.caveat: The quote is JADAM liquid fertilizer at its standard 1:100 dilution, not the 1:10 comfrey tea. v2 uses it only to say whether the full-requirement tea volume fits a normal liquid application.

source.quote: Grass clippings are a cheap, effective mulch. Apply them at a maximum depth of 5cm (2in) or the heat they create as they decompose may harm the stems.

mulch_depth_cm.caveat: The 5 cm maximum is for grass clippings; coarser or drier materials can be applied deeper (the corpus also describes 8-12 inch sheet mulch). v2 reports it as the default fresh-material mulch depth.

source.quote: Matches the existing bioaccumulator_oracle.py ratio rounding.
Six decimals keeps small standard-rate batches visible while staying stable across Python and Dart double arithmetic.
